source: The lack of evidence in our study for eIF2A function in translation initiation stands in contrast to findings of negative genetic interactions between the eIF2AΔ and mutations in yeast eIF4E (Komar et al., 2005) and eIF5B (Zoll et al., 2002) wherein combining the mutations conferred a more severe cell growth defect.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Komar et al., 2005 and Zoll et al., 2002.

claim: Synthetic negative interactions between eIF2AΔ and deletions of each of the two genes encoding eIF4A (TIF1 and TIF2) were reported in a global analysis of synthetic phenotypes.
source: Synthetic negative interactions between eIF2AΔ and deletions of each of the two genes encoding eIF4A (TIF1 and TIF2) were also reported in a global analysis of synthetic phenotypes observed in double mutants that combine deletions or point mutations in ~90% of all yeast genes (Costanzo et al., 2016; van Leeuwen et al., 2016), compiled at https://thecellmap.org/costanzo2016/.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Costanzo et al., 2016 and van Leeuwen et al., 2016.

claim: One possibility is that eIF2A is functionally redundant with eIF4E, eIF4A, and eIF5B rather than with eIF2.
source: One possibility is that eIF2A is functionally redundant with these initiation factors rather than with eIF2.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the genetic interaction data.

claim: Another possibility is that eliminating eIF2A affects a different cellular process and that expression of one or more genes involved in that process is diminished by mutations in eIF4E, –4A, and –5B.
source: Another is that eliminating eIF2A affects a different cellular process and that expression of one or more genes involved in that process is diminished by mutations in eIF4E, –4A, and –5B.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the genetic interaction data.

claim: Human recombinant eIF2A inhibits translation in rabbit reticulocyte lysate (RRL) of all mRNAs tested, including one driven by the cricket paralysis virus IGR IRES that requires no canonical initiation factors.
source: A recent study indicated that human recombinant eIF2A inhibits translation in rabbit reticulocyte lysate (RRL) of all mRNAs tested, including one driven by the cricket paralysis virus IGR IRES that requires no canonical initiation factors (Grove et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Grove et al., 2023.

claim: Human eIF2A binds to 40S subunits and the addition of excess 40S subunits to RRL mitigates its inhibitory effect.
source: Because the protein binds to 40S subunits and the addition of excess 40S subunits to RRL mitigates its inhibitory effect, it was concluded that human eIF2A sequestered 40S subunits in an inactive complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by a reference to findings from Grove et al., 2023.

claim: The finding that eIF2AΔ does not increase bulk translation or impact yeast cell growth suggests that eIF2A does not appreciably sequester 40S ribosomes in yeast cells, even in stress conditions of eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: While this finding is consistent with the conclusion that yeast eIF2A represses IRES-driven translation in yeast, the finding that eIF2AΔ does not increase bulk translation or impact yeast cell growth obtained here and elsewhere (Zoll et al., 2002) suggests that eIF2A does not appreciably sequester 40S ribosomes in yeast cells, even in stress conditions of eIF2α phosphorylation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the polysome profiling data and a citation to Zoll et al., 2002.

claim: Knocking out the eIF2A gene had no detectable effect on bulk translation in keratinocytes.
source: The similar finding that knocking out the eIF2A gene had no detectable effect on bulk translation in keratinocytes (Sendoel et al., 2017) led Grove et al., 2023 to surmise that mammalian eIF2A is not normally present in the cytoplasm and would have to be released from a different cellular compartment to impact translation (Grove et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sendoel et al., 2017 and Grove et al., 2023.

claim: It is surprising that so little evidence was found that eIF2A functions in the yeast translatome even when the activity of the canonical factor eIF2 is attenuated by amino acid starvation.
source: It is surprising that we found so little evidence that eIF2A functions in the yeast translatome even when the activity of the canonical factor eIF2 is attenuated by amino acid starvation.
evidence: This is a summary statement reflecting on the overall findings of the study.

claim: It is possible that eIF2A plays a more important role in translation in some other stress condition, for example, one in which it is released into the cytoplasm or when eIF4E or eIF5B function is attenuated.
source: It is possible that eIF2A plays a more important role in translation in some other stress condition, for example, one in which it is released into the cytoplasm (Grove et al., 2023) or when eIF4E or eIF5B function is attenuated, or that it functions in a different cellular process altogether in budding yeast.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible alternative roles for eIF2A.

claim: eIF2A may have acquired a new role in controlling translation initiation during mammalian evolution, or it could have lost its function in translation and acquired a different one during fungal evolution.
source: eIF2A may have acquired a new role in controlling translation initiation during mammalian evolution, or it could have lost its function in translation and acquired a different one during fungal evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the evolutionary trajectory of eIF2A function.
